method: Independent solve from each newly added blind question, its printed options, packet-provided source excerpts, and official syllabus excerpt only. No sealed author artifact, answer map, or prior solution was opened.

items.subject: accountancy
items.calculation: Common-size expense share = expense / revenue × 100. P: 600/800 × 100 = 75%. Q: 160/200 × 100 = 80%. P has the lower expense share.

source_support.support: Common-size statements express each item as a percentage of a common item and allow inter-firm comparisons.
For a profit-and-loss common-size statement, expenditure items are percentages of revenue from operations.

syllabus_support.unit: Unit V: Analysis of Financial Statements
syllabus_support.topic: Tools for Financial Analysis: Common size statements.

option_review.A: Correct: P is 75% and Q is 80%, so P has the lower share.
option_review.B: Incorrect: compares absolute rupee expenses (₹600 versus ₹160) rather than shares of revenue; Q's share is actually higher.
option_review.C: Incorrect: reverses the two calculated percentages and the resulting comparison.
option_review.D: Incorrect: being below revenue does not make the shares equal; they are 75% and 80%.

items.subject: economics
items.calculation: Marginal cost for the increase from 3 to 4 units = change in total cost / change in output = (₹49−₹44)/(4−3) = ₹5 per unit.

source_support.support: The excerpt defines short-run marginal cost as change in total cost per unit change in output.

items.subject: economics
items.calculation: Total cost = fixed cost + variable cost. TC rises from ₹20+₹60=₹80 to ₹20+₹75=₹95. For one additional unit, SMC = (₹95−₹80)/(9−8) = ₹15 per unit; equivalently, fixed cost is unchanged so the ₹15 increase in variable cost is the total-cost increase.

source_support.support: The excerpt states TC = TVC + TFC and explains that fixed cost stays constant while variable cost changes with output.
The excerpt defines short-run marginal cost as change in total cost per unit change in output.
